data.narrative:
Agile Robots, a Series C robotics and manufacturing company, has raised approximately $384M to date against a stated valuation exceeding $1.0B. The comparable universe consists of nine private robotics firms at Series B through Series D stages—including Exotec ($2.0B, Series D), Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B, Series B), Hadrian ($1.6B, Series C), and Dexterity ($1.6B, Series B)—plus one public comparable (277810.KQ).

Two valuation methods were applied. The stage-progression approach uses the $1.0B last post-money valuation as a base and applies a 1.7x multiplier typical of Series C-to-next-stage step-ups, yielding $1.7B. The peer-median method examines six same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables, which trade at a median valuation of $1.7B with a range of $1.0B to $2.0B. Both methods converge on identical point estimates.

The triangulated valuation range is $1.4B to $2.0B, with a median of $1.7B. This range reflects consistency between stage-based progression and peer-relative positioning. Key uncertainties include execution risk relative to later-stage peers, competitive dynamics within the rapidly expanding robotics sector, and revenue traction relative to deployed capital. The peer set spans multiple deployment contexts and technology approaches, suggesting modest comparability risk but warranting deeper revenue and unit economics review.
